content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper attempts to make 2 contributions: (1) an RL approach aiming at a variety of diverse problems in quant finance which the authors call AlphaMix++, which combines a collection of base RL algorithms using a mixture-of-experts approach, and adds risk-sensitivity by modifying the bellman equation.  (2) A framework for evaluating RL algorithms in finance which includes datasets, example RL methods, and a dashboard that compares various metrics from performance (returns, risk),  comprehensiveness of evaluation (how many markets has the methods been evaluated on), and soft measures like reliability, interpretability, and diversity.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: The topic of RL reproducibility is an important one, and a well-executed suite of quant-trading RL benchmarks and methods (in the style of stable-baselines) could be a useful resource for the RL community as an additional application, if done well.  Risk-aware RL with a mixture of diverse agents sounds like a reasonable direction (however, the paper lacks details and relevant scholarship to judge its soundness and novelty).

Weaknesses:  Unfortunately the paper severely lacks in most aspects -- writing, scholarship, soundness, evaluation.  It tries to cover a lot of territory -- it seems almost like a brain-dump of everything that the authors could think about on the topic, and it spreads itself too thin. Attention to detail is minimal. The paper probably should've been a desk-reject in the current shape.  

I'll list some example issues:
a) Notation is used without ever being defined. Equations (2) and (3) and (4) -- almost none of the key symbols are ever defined / introduced. Some can be guessed, but e.g. new risk-aware RL concepts Q-bar-std and such definitely should be defined.  At any rate readers are not in the guessing game - papers should be self-consistent. 
b) Poor scholarship: various facts and quotes are stated without references (prevalence of algo-trading, quote by David Shaw, etc),  lack of references to risk-aware RL (this is different from policies encouraging exploration which are reasonably cited) -- it's a big and complicated topic.  It's unclear if the main proposal for a "FinRL" agent AlphaMix++ exists in the literature or it's a contribution of the paper. In any case it's not properly described in the paper. 
c) Lack of any useful details in evaluation.  RL methods were run for trading on US, chinese data, Crypto and FX.  What stocks, what years, what time stamps (milli-seconds or weeks?) how did you prepare and clean the data -- all of this is missing. This is utterly unacceptable for an application where the devil is in the details, here no details are provided whatsoever. 
d) Comparing 'fluctuated financial markets' to 'StartCraft II, Go and Nuclear fusion' -- as similar -- shows the level of market knowledge and attention to detail.  There are very limited details on algo-trading / portfolio management / market making and order execution.  Lumping them into a general quant-finance category skips any useful distinction (time-horizons, amount and type of available data, e.t.c). Portfolio is defined only as weights that sum to one -- how do you keep track of the size?  10k USD portfolio vs 1B USD portfolio with same proportions behave very differently. 
e) The evaluation also makes little sense -- are you evaluating method performance or coverage of experiments that the method was subjected, how do you create a combined score by merging together various metrics...  What does it mean to evaluate t-SNE of a method, and correlation? Are you correlating performance metrics of different methods or of the data-sets, is diversity for methods or data-sets? It seems PRUDEX-compass includes anything and everything even tangentially relevant that the authors could think about,  thrown into a coarse blender and mixed together to produce a colorful smorgasbord of a dashboard display.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Please see above.  Severe issues in clarity, quality and reproducibility.  This is especially concerning since the aim is at reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: Topic of reproducible RL with applications in quant-finance could be interesting, but paper lacks in all aspects.
content.correctness: 1: The main claims of the paper are incorrect or not at all supported by theory or empirical results.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
The submission studies quantitative trading. The key challenge the submission aims to solve is the evaluation of methods in QT. To this end, the authors propose PRUDEX-Compass, a framework to evaluate portfolio optimization methods from 6 different perspectives. 

The submission also provides a new portfolio optimization method, AlphaMix+. This method conducts ensemble learning and has better characteristics compared to some existing ones. 

The usage of both PRUDEX-Compass and AlphaMix+ is demonstrated on four tasks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength

The submission considers a very motivating question, the evaluation of methods in QT. 

The submission is easy to follow with informative demo figures. 

Weakness

1. On the high level, PRUDEX-Compass and AlphaMix+ are not consistently unified. PRUDEX-Compass is an evaluation framework, while AlphaMix+ is a new QT method leveraging ensemble. Is there any deeper connection between the two? For example, is the motivation of AlphaMix+ an easier evaluation? Or, is AlphaMix+ specifically designed for PRUDEX-Compass? Right now the AlphaMix+ part does not seem to be very relevant to PRUDEX-Compass. 

Would it be possible for authors strengthen the connection between PRUDEX-Compass and AlphaMix+ or just focus on one of the two? 

2. The contribution of PRUDEX-Compass seems to be limited. First of all, all the measures in PRUDEX-Compass seem to be some existing easy-to-calculate evaluation metrics. While it is convenient to have all this calculation provided in one package, there does not seem to be a big methodological contribution or any real challenges in doing so. Second, I am not quite sure whether having more evaluation metrics is the key to a systematic evaluation. In other words, while I agree the systematic evaluation for methods in QT is hard and important, but the key challenge to me is the distribution shift in the problem instead of lacking more evaluation metrics. In existing works, something like a sharpe ratio or CARA utility function is enough to evaluate the performance of a portfolio. The hard part is to estimate such metrics correctly using the historical data with potential distribution shift.  

3. The contribution of AlphaMix+ also seems to be limited. I am wondering what might be the performance difference between just ensemble on some QT methods compared to AlphaMix+? If we can achieve similar performances but just ensemble learning, it does not seem to be very necessary to propose a new methodology for it. 

4. For section 2.2, are we assuming the actions can affect asset prices? Or the actions can only affect wealth or the position on an asset? If the action can only affect the wealth, why do we need a critic? Given a policy, can we just calculate/simulate the wealth process and conduct backpropagation through the wealth? If the action can affect other variables, how can we observe the actions in the dataset to learn the action effects? 

For 2, 3, and 4, would it be possible for authors to further motivate the proposed methods? For example, what are the major contributions of PRUDEX-Compass except providing more evaluation metrics? How the provided more evaluation metrics can lead to a more systematic and better evaluation framework than existing ones? What are the methodological innovations of AlphaMix+?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity
The submission is clearly written and easy to follow. The main writing issue is that PRUDEX-Compass and AlphaMix+ are not well unified. 

Novelty
I cannot well follow the novelty of the proposed method for now. The main reason is discussed in comment 2, 3, 4. 

Reproducibility
The reproducibility of the submission is good.
content.summary_of_the_review: Currently, I find the submission not well motivated. To address the comment 1, 2, 3, and 4, I believe there need to be some major changes to the submission.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper presents PRUDEX-compass which contains 6 measures to benchmark FinRL algorithms. The paper also proposed a new method AlphaMix+ based on DRL for risk aware investment decisions as a potential baseline.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
- The paper presents an important metric for comparing and benchmarking FinRL algorithms. The idea of visually presenting and comparing algorithm is highly appreciated. 
- The paper is well written and explains the techniques very well. The authors have done commendable job in providing sufficient details. However, details of AlphaMix+ are not provided for reproducibility in the main text. This is important for readers to reproduce the results based on these details. 

Weaknesses: 
- The paper fails to provide all sufficient details of AlphaMix+. For example, an algorithm can be added for providing step wise details of the proposed approach. 
- Figure 4.3 shows t-SNE plot of market data. The scatter makes sense but is the main use of this with respect to the proposed metric? The authors have not given any clue how does it help in PRUDEX or AlphaMix+ 
- All notations must be defined in the main text. For example, what does beta mean in equation 2. Similarly, many more such instances. 
- One common problem in using this visualization is the proper comparable metric. For example, profitability is a general term. Both accounting and cashflow based PnL can be used here. A method can be good in accounting PnL and another could be better in cashflow PnL metric. How will the comparison reflect in this sense?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is very clear in stating all requirements and problem statement, however, there are issues with notations but can be corrected. The paper proposes a new metric which is significantly novel to be used for benchmarking FinRL algorithms.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper is good in most of the aspects but more details of AlphaMix+ is required for reader to reproduce the results. See strengths and weaknesses for further justification.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces PRUDEX-Compass, an evaluation framework for RL-based models for four tasks in finance, namely algorithmic trading, portfolio management, order execution, and market making. The authors also propose AlphaMix+, a MoE algorithm, realized by weighted Q-learning loss, and demonstrate that it is a strong baseline under PRUDEX-Compass.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
* Strength 

(i) The work is well motivated -- as far as I know, there is not such a framework exist for evaluating RL models for multiple finance tasks.

(ii) The framework itself is comprehensive, as it covers a good amount of measurements that practitioners care.

(iii) The proposed model, AlphaMix+, appears to be well designed, and the use of standard deviation for reweighting, along with bootstrapping, seems to be novel.

* Weakness

(i) "We perform all experiments on an RTX 3090 GPU with 5 fixed random seeds. We apply grid search for AlphaMix+ to find suitable hyperparameters (details in Appendix D.4), where it takes about 30 minutes to train each random seed. For other FinRL methods, we follow their default settings in public implementations (Liu et al., 2020a) to keep a fair comparison" -- to ensure a fair comparison, other baselines should also follow the same tuning procedure for hyper-parameters.

(ii) Why only AlphaMix+ is evaluated for almost all of the items in the outer-level?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Quality and clarity is good. Originality is less relevant. Reproducibility is good.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall I think it is a good benchmark paper, while the documentation for the code is still missing is the current release.
